title: Waste cart contract and Highland Road housing land sale
subtitle: Also: taxi meter rate increase, New Dundee roundabout, committee renaming, Greenfield Avenue housing transfer, and Wilmot land assembly delegations.
overview: Regional Council approved an eight-year automated cart-based waste collection contract with Emterra Environmental starting in March 2026, and accepted a proposal from Savic Homes to buy surplus land at 1388 Highland Road West in Kitchener for affordable housing. Council also raised the taxi meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50 {{vote:m13}} and approved a roundabout at New Dundee Road and Strasburg Road, along with new pedestrian crossovers and speed changes on several regional roads.

Council accepted the transfer of the 595 Greenfield Avenue community housing project into Waterloo Region Housing {{vote:m15}}. It also approved a property purchase tied to the River Road extension, and the 2023 consolidated financial statements {{vote:m17}}. Council renamed the Planning and Works committee the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Standing Committee {{vote:m21}}. The change takes effect at the August committee cycle.

Delegations spoke about the Wilmot Township land assembly and a petition on policing and homelessness. Public Health reported progress on school immunization records. Closed-session items were reported only through later motions, such as a land sale for a school walkway on Lauris Avenue in Cambridge.

decisions.detail: Council accepted Emterra Environmental's proposal for automated cart-based and manual waste collection for eight years from March 2026, with two optional one-year renewals, as part of the Planning and Works summary.
Council accepted Savic Homes' proposal for surplus Region land at 1388 Highland Road West in Kitchener and authorized the sale agreement.
Council amended the taxi by-law to raise the meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50.
Council approved the design of a multi-lane roundabout at New Dundee Road and Strasburg Road, with speed limit and lane changes after construction.

decisions.item: Greenfield Avenue housing transfer and River Road property
decisions.detail: Council accepted the transfer of the 595 Greenfield Avenue community housing project into Waterloo Region Housing, authorized buying 333-339 Hidden Valley Road for $4,300,000, and advanced River Road extension funding to 2024.
Council accepted Capital Paving's tender for Ottawa Street improvements between Fischer-Hallman Road and Mowat Boulevard and approved a project cost increase of $573,300 gross and $0 net.
Council renamed the Planning and Works committee the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Standing Committee.
Council approved a rent framework for Waterloo Region Housing community spaces and revised terms of reference for the Public Art Advisory Committee.

debate: Several councillors questioned the new waste carts. One worried about bin dimensions and where residents with small garages, stacked townhouses or apartments above stores would keep them. Staff said the carts are an industry-standard size, that the Region covers their cost, and that downtown collection is being studied separately.

Staff argued that rejecting the contract would mean a new request for proposals for manual pickup, likely with few bidders and higher costs. Other councillors said carts had worked well in other municipalities and at their own cottages. The councillor who raised the concern chose not to move a deferral but asked for the dimensions to be shared.

On the Highland Road land, one councillor asked why the Region was selling rather than leasing the land. Staff said the land's equity is needed to finance the project and secure about 40 years of affordability, and that leasing may suit other sites.

Two delegates from Wilmot opposed the land assembly there. They cited a lack of public consultation and communication, uncertainty for farmers, effects on water quality and transportation, and loss of prime farmland. One suggested the Region look for willing sellers closer to the cities.

A delegation backing the Fightback KW petition called for a five-year freeze on police budget increases, a halt to construction at 100 Victoria Street until there are enough housing solutions, and a review of the shelter system.
